faqs.question: What does Threonine Quantitative Urine Test measure?
faqs.answer: The Threonine Quantitative Urine Test measures the amount of threonine in your newborn's urine sample.

faqs.question: Why is Threonine Quantitative Urine Test done?
faqs.answer: • To identify metabolic disorders that affect the threonine pathway • To detect inborn errors of metabolism • To detect vitamin B6 insufficiency

faqs.question: When is the Threonine Test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: • If your doctor suspects any metabolic disorder or inborn errors of metabolism, they may order this test. Common indications include muscle weakness, developmental delay, or liver disease. • Newborns are also tested to detect metabolic disorders that can cause serious health problems early on.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Threonine Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Elevated levels may indicate metabolic disorders such as liver disease, multiple sclerosis, or even cancer. Low levels could indicate malnutrition or digestive issues.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Threonine Urine Test?
faqs.answer: • Provide a 10-ml spot urine sample of your newborn. • The sample will be taken to a laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Threonine Test?
faqs.answer: • Follow the fasting recommendations of your doctor. • Stop amino acid supplementation or medication for some time before the test. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Threonine Test?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the Threonine Quantitative Urine Test include complete blood count, liver function tests, and other urine organic acid tests.

faqs.question: What is the Threonine Quantitative Urine Test also known as?
faqs.answer: Quantitative amino acid threonine analysis of urine

faqs.question: What is metabolic disorder?
faqs.answer: Metabolic disorders occur when abnormal chemical reactions in the body disrupt normal metabolic processes. These disorders can impact an individual's ability to process certain nutrients and can lead to various health issues including digestion problems, organ dysfunction, and developmental delay.
